verdict.summary: HubSpot apps are built as projects. You configure distribution, auth, scopes and redirect URLs in app-hsmeta.json and upload with the HubSpot CLI. A Marketplace-distribution OAuth app works for up to 25 customer accounts with no review. Past that, it must be reviewed and listed by HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, which requires 3 active installs and does an initial review within 10 business days.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 h to a working app; ~1 day for listing materials
verdict.approval_wait: none for up to 25 installs; listing: initial review within 10 business days, whole process up to ~60 days

gates.name: Developer test accounts
gates.unlocks: Install in developer test accounts, which don't count toward any install limit.

gates.name: Unlisted Marketplace-distribution app (or private allowlist)
gates.unlocks: Real customer accounts can install via OAuth: up to 25 accounts for Marketplace distribution before listing, or 10 allowlisted accounts for private distribution.
limits: 25-install cap until reviewed and listed (Marketplace distribution).
Installers need the App Marketplace Access permission when the app requests new scopes.

gates.name: Listed on the HubSpot Marketplace
limits: Requires 3+ active installs from unaffiliated production accounts (activity in the past 30 days).
Only one app can be under review at a time.

steps.title: Get a HubSpot account with developer access
steps.detail: Sign up through HubSpot's developer signup. In our probe, the developer signup URL redirected to HubSpot's standard CRM signup with intent=developer.

steps.title: Create the app project and set distribution + auth
steps.detail: Create a project with the HubSpot CLI. In app-hsmeta.json choose OAuth auth and Marketplace (or private) distribution, list only the scopes you need, and add redirectUrls. An agent can generate this config.

values.label: redirectUrls
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's default HubSpot scope set has 33 scopes, including settings.users.write and crm.export. Trim it, because every new scope forces customers to have App Marketplace Access to install.

steps.title: Upload the project
steps.detail: Run hs project upload. The same command applies later changes such as new redirect URLs.

steps.title: Connect a developer test account through Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and secret into a Composio auth config for HubSpot (OAuth2) and install into a developer test account.

steps.title: Onboard design partners (up to 25)
steps.detail: Customers install via your OAuth flow. Make sure each installer has the App Marketplace Access permission in their HubSpot account.
gotchas: The 26th install is blocked until the app is listed.

steps.title: Prepare the listing
steps.detail: An agent can draft the listing copy and check that your Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs are live. Allowlist the 'HubSpot Crawler' user agent on your site to avoid delays.
gotchas: You need at least 3 active installs from unaffiliated production accounts.

steps.title: Submit and respond to feedback
steps.detail: The Ecosystem Quality team does an initial review within 10 business days; the full review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared.
gotchas: Submitting a second app while one is in review auto-rejects the second.

requirements.item: Live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs

requirements.detail: Production accounts with app activity in the past 30 days.

scopes.effect: Typical CRM scopes; any new scope requires installers to have App Marketplace Access.
In Composio's defaults; admin-level, so drop it unless needed.

blockers.symptom: New customer can't install: install limit reached
blockers.cause: Unlisted Marketplace-distribution apps are capped at 25 installs.
blockers.fix: Get listed (3 active installs + review), or remove inactive installs.
blockers.contact: HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team (via listing submission)

blockers.cause: Installing an app that requests new scopes needs the App Marketplace Access permission.
blockers.fix: Ask a HubSpot super admin to grant the permission or perform the install.

composio.note: Prototype on Composio's managed HubSpot app. Your own app's real constraint is the 25-install cap, not approval, so start the listing process once you pass about 10 customers.

evidence.claim: Distribution and auth settings live in app-hsmeta.json; redirect URLs change via redirectUrls + hs project upload; private OAuth apps: up to 10 allowlisted accounts; Marketplace-distribution OAuth apps: up to 25 accounts before listing, unlimited after; developer test accounts excluded.
evidence.quote: can be installed in up to 25 accounts (not including developer test accounts)

evidence.claim: The 25-install cap applies until the app is reviewed by the Ecosystem Quality team and listed.
evidence.quote: until your app is reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and listed on the Marketplace

evidence.claim: Installing an app that requests new OAuth scopes requires the App Marketplace Access permission.
evidence.quote: The App Marketplace Access permission will be required to install an app any time an app requests new OAuth scopes.

evidence.claim: Listing: initial review within 10 business days; process ≤60 days from feedback; ≥3 active unaffiliated installs; live ToS/Privacy Policy; allowlist HubSpot Crawler; one app in review at a time.
evidence.quote: the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days

evidence.claim: Composio's HubSpot toolkit is managed (OAUTH2) with 33 default scopes including settings.users.write and crm.export.
HubSpot's developer signup URL redirects to the standard signup with intent=developer.
HubSpot's authorize endpoint is reachable (renders a JavaScript 'HubSpot OAuth' page for an unknown client).

open_questions: Older listing docs mention a 'Technology Partner Program' instead of 'Marketplace'; wording varies by page version.
Whether the developer signup now creates a standard account with developer features rather than a separate developer account (suggested by the redirect) was not confirmed in docs.
